rebuilds.why: Round-2 fix for the HOLD: RAN made BRAND, and 'a long white brand on his chin' is defensible (a burned mark), so the row had two defensible answers. RAN replaced with OAR, which makes BOARD; a board cannot be on a chin under any reading. Execution and walk script updated to match; the walk no longer relies on 'grow' to rule out the distractor. Key EAR/BEARD, ELO/BELOD and the sentence are unchanged.

stem.prompt: Three letters are missing from the word in capitals. Together they spell a word. Which three?
stem.sentence: Grandad has a long white B___D on his chin.

options.execution: OAR is itself a word and makes BOARD, a real word, but a board is not something a person has on their chin. Tagged ignores-sentence: the child built a word without checking the sentence.
ELO is not a word, and in the gap it makes BELOD, which is not a word either. Tagged fits-gap-not-word: the child filled the gap without using the little-word rule.

explanationPatch.walkScript: “elo” is not a word, so it cannot be the answer. “oar” makes “board”, but nobody has a board on their chin. “ear” makes “beard”, the hair that grows on a chin.
